observations:
Torah #77 (LM2) is a tightly structured Torah with a clear three-package architecture that fully accounts for all bechina-connected nodes in the dataset.

The three packages are:
1. Package 1 (Da'at/Mochin/Binyamin/Tefillin) — the intellectual domain, 'good' polarity
2. Package 2 (Yirah/Malkhut/Yehudah/Strap cluster) — the fear/malkhut domain, 'good' polarity
3. Package 3 (Fallen Yirah/Evil Strap) — the evil mirror, 'evil' polarity

No independent bechina domain of 3+ concepts emerges from the source text beyond these three clusters. The remaining major concepts in the Torah are:

(a) EITZA-ONLY concepts: אכילה בקדשה (eating in holiness) is the central practical mechanism of the Torah but appears only as an eitza cause-node, not in any bechina equation. It flows between packages rather than belonging to one.

(b) RESULT-CONCEPTS: קומת אדם (human stature of the mouth), אדם העליון (supernal Adam), שכינה מדברת מתוך גרונו (the Shekhinah speaking from his throat) — these are the culminating states that the Torah leads to via eitza. While the Rebbe uses bechina language for them ('this is the bechina of supernal Adam'), they do not form an independent thematic domain separate from Package 2; they are extensions of the yirah/malkhut domain reaching its highest expression. They are better understood as additions to Package 2 (as noted in torah_77_additions.json) rather than constituting a new independent package.

(c) The AGGADIC NARRATIVE (the tzaddik of Binyamin's lot who grieved daily over the strap crossing into Yehudah's territory and sought to swallow it) is explicitly decoded as a parable for the entire teaching. Its nodes (the tzaddik's daily grief, his seeking to sweeten it through eating, his becoming an אושפיזכן for the Shekhinah) are eitza-narrative nodes, not independent bechina clusters.

Conclusion: The existing three packages exhaust the bechina topology of this Torah. No fourth independent conceptual domain is present.
